problem:
Consider the initial value problem 

$$
{y}^{′}=y(x-1),\,y(0)=2.
$$

Use the tangent line approximation of $y(x)$ at $x=0$ to approximate $y(1).$ Do not round the answer.

$y(1)≈$  
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation to $y(x)$ at the point $a=0$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =y(a)+{y}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =y(0)+{y}^{′}(0)(x-0).\end{aligned}
$$

From the initial condition, we know that $y(0)=2.$ We also know that ${y}^{′}(x)=y(x-1),$ so

$$
{y}^{′}(0)=2(0-1)=-2.
$$

Substituting our values for $y(0)$ and ${y}^{′}(0)$ into our expression for $L(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =y(0)+{y}^{′}(0)(x-0) \\  & =2+(-2)(x-0) \\  & =2-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can approximate $y(1)$ using $L(1).$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}y(1) & ≈L(1) \\  & =2-2(1) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
